issues.failure_explanation: The claimed invariance of S fails. Let B_1 = ([\;]_0 [\;]_1)_0 and B_2 = ([\;]_1 [\;]_0)_0; then B_1 and B_2 are distinct LN-trees with B_1 ~ B_2 (branch swap) and |B_1| = |B_2| = 4. The trees Upsilon = (B_1 B_2)_0 and Upsilon' = (B_1 B_1)_0 both have order 9 and satisfy Upsilon ~ Upsilon' (since B_2 ~ B_1), but S(Upsilon) = N_P(Upsilon) S(B_1) S(B_2) = 1*1*1 = 1 (no nontrivial permutation preserves the sequence (B_1, B_2)) while S(Upsilon') = 2*1*1 = 2. Hence prop_Labs_equ (ii) is false in general; the extension of S to ULN-trees in def_func_Ntree is representative-dependent for trees of order >= 9, and the ULN-level expansion coefficient alpha(Upsilon) S(Upsilon)/gamma(Upsilon) in eq2_Rnj_indc is incorrect for r >= 9 (the correct class aggregate is gamma(Upsilon)^{-1} sum_{Upsilon' in [Upsilon]} S(Upsilon')/N_P(Upsilon')). For r <= 8 (in particular all tabulated cases r <= 5) the invariance does hold: a class containing members with different N_P requires two branches drawn from a nontrivial equivalence class, and the smallest such branch class has order 4, forcing order >= 9.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the ULN-level coefficient alpha(Upsilon) S(Upsilon)/gamma(Upsilon) in eq2_Rnj_indc by the class aggregate gamma(Upsilon)^{-1} sum_{Upsilon' in [Upsilon]} S(Upsilon')/N_P(Upsilon') (which simultaneously repairs ISSUE-002), and drop S from the invariance claim in prop_Labs_equ (ii); alternatively restrict the general statements to r <= 8 where S is class-invariant.
issues.overall_effect: prop_Labs_equ (ii) is false; the symmetry order S on ULN-trees (def_func_Ntree) is ill-defined for trees of order >= 9; the ULN form of the error expansion in thm_taylor (eq2_Rnj_indc) has an incorrect coefficient for r >= 9. The tabulated cases r <= 5 and all order conditions are unaffected.
issues.title: Symmetry order S is not invariant under the LN-tree equivalence relation
issues.why_classification: The false invariance claim and the resulting ill-definedness of S on ULN-trees only affect the general-r statement for r >= 9; every tabulated case (r <= 5) and every downstream result (order conditions, consistency, convergence) is unaffected, and the repair is a contained coefficient replacement requiring no new proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: Passing from eq_estEtniDelFtnij to eq_estDelFtnij requires E[rho^2(Etnj{eta} - Etni{eta})] <= E[rho^2(eta)] - E[rho^2(Etn{eta})] with eta = Delta Theta^{n+1}. For a Euclidean seminorm this follows from Pythagoras (E|eta - Etn eta|^2 = E|eta|^2 - E|Etn eta|^2 and E|Etni eta|^2 >= E|Etn eta|^2 by the tower property), but it is false for a general seminorm: with rho(theta) = ||theta_y||_infinity, eta = (X_1+1, X_2) with X_1, X_2 i.i.d. N(0,1) and trivial F_{t_n}, E[rho^2(eta - Etn eta)] = E[max(X_1^2, X_2^2)] = 1 + 2/pi ~ 1.637, while E[rho^2(eta)] - E[rho^2(Etn eta)] = E[max((X_1+1)^2, X_2^2)] - 1 ~ 1.479. Since assu_FLipVar permits a general seminorm, lemm_LipVarRK and thm_rk_stable are unproven as stated for general seminorms.
